object.role: nearby coeval open-cluster calibration ensemble with extended tidal tails

semanticAudit.configurationT1: exploratory locally dominant electromagnetic/null transport sector; only meaning admitted to the spike
semanticAudit.modularT1: genus-two theta-characteristic transformation; not a celestial vector and has no defined angle to M44
semanticAudit.ordinaryTailAxis: spatial or phase-space principal direction; measurable but not identified with configuration T1

exactResults.constantSpectralAngle: not identifiable separately from systemic radial velocity in the declared single-channel model
exactResults.unknownHiddenRatio: only combinations of q and theta enter one projected frequency record
exactResults.spatialAngle: not identifiable from observed cluster covariance without an independently fixed intrinsic covariance

ordinarySpatialControl.method: tangent-plane PCA with x=(RA-meanRA)*cos(meanDec), y=Dec-meanDec; covariance normalized by N
ordinarySpatialControl.interpretation: ordinary sky-plane catalogue axis only; not a configuration T1 measurement

crossChannelDiagnostic.status: executed exploratory diagnostic; reproducible residual structure detected; physical attribution open
crossChannelDiagnostic.astrometryAndSpectroscopySource: Gaia DR3 gaia_source joined through dr2_neighbourhood
crossChannelDiagnostic.method: fit one ICRS space-velocity vector from Gaia DR3 proper motions and parallaxes without spectroscopic RV; predict astrometric RV; subtract from Gaia DR3 spectroscopic RV; regress robust-inlier residuals on signed published-catalogue PCA coordinate anchored at the median cluster centre

frozenModelGate.corpusNativeT1Model: r(s)=a; cluster-wide theta and q enter only as a constant projection factor and are predictively identical to the intercept-only null
frozenModelGate.reason: the corpus supplies no theta(s) evolution law, boundary condition or coupling kernel from which a spatial derivative can be predicted
frozenModelGate.ordinarySurrogate: r(s)=a+b*s; literature-motivated linear tail-velocity trend, not a replacement for the published N-body particle model
frozenModelGate.comparisonStatus: retrospective five-fold rehearsal; not confirmatory because the aggregate gradient was inspected before the split and model freeze
frozenModelGate.training: Theil-Sen line for ordinary surrogate; training median for constant comparator
frozenModelGate.interpretation: a linear spatial kinematic term generalizes slightly better than a constant offset; this does not identify its physical cause and supplies no evidence for T1

alternativeShapeTournament.status: retrospective nested five-fold hypothesis discovery; not confirmatory
alternativeShapeTournament.coordinate: signed angular coordinate along the published-catalogue sky-plane principal axis
alternativeShapeTournament.result: spatial structure generalizes versus a constant offset, but no tested boundary or relaxation shape is distinguishable from an ordinary linear tail term
alternativeShapeTournament.nextDiscriminator: three-dimensional tail position with uncertainty, frozen ordinary phase-space predictions, or untouched spectroscopy outside the current angular window

threeDimensionalTailAndSpectralSurface.method: heliocentric Cartesian positions from Gaia DR3 sky direction and inverse parallax; robust component-wise median centre; principal covariance axis from all 1247 selected members; axis sign aligned to the published sky-plane tail coordinate
threeDimensionalTailAndSpectralSurface.uncertaintyBoundary: 2000 deterministic Gaussian perturbations of along-axis coordinate from reported parallax error; membership, common-velocity fit, correlations and PCA axis held fixed

spectralControl.interpretation: the spatial term survives a coarse Gaia RV-template-temperature control; aggregate catalogue RV cannot test line-by-line carrier coherence

threeDimensionalTailAndSpectralSurface.surface: 12 equal-count robust-inlier bins along the 3-D tail and 28 populated tail-by-template-temperature cells are emitted by the analysis runner
threeDimensionalTailAndSpectralSurface.interpretation: three-dimensional spatial structure is present in this reconstruction but does not identify boundary topology or T1 coupling

exceptionalDirectionCandidate.status: retrospective ordinary-data candidate-direction scan; not a T1 identification or confirmatory holdout
exceptionalDirectionCandidate.model: r(x)=a+g dot (x-mean(x)) using inverse-parallax heliocentric Cartesian positions
exceptionalDirectionCandidate.result: the ordinary residual field contains a modest reproducible three-dimensional directional term beyond the tail coordinate
exceptionalDirectionCandidate.interpretation: freeze as an ordinary candidate or nuisance axis for independent data; perspective-model error, tail curvature, binaries, catalogue systematics and ordinary dynamics remain sufficient explanations

orientationPriorControl.reason: no source-native law maps ordinary cluster size, shape, formation plane or tidal-tail axis to configuration-T1 orientation
orientationPriorControl.visibilityConstraint: at 90 degrees the rank-two common plane remains visible and only the exceptional component vanishes; total brightness does not disfavor orthogonality, while a carrier independently assigned to the exceptional direction would provide a constraint
orientationPriorControl.verdict: near-90 angles may have more prior measure under isotropic 3-D axes, but M44 morphology and total brightness supply no posterior preference; a resolved exceptional-direction carrier is required

spiralInclinationSlicingTemplate.convention: external-galaxy inclination i=0 is face-on and i=90 is edge-on

conditionalTailAsT1.status: geometric conditional only; the tail axis is not identified with configuration T1

spiralInclinationSlicingTemplate.placement: M44 is an intermediate approximately 58-degree sightline slice in the Solar/Local-Arm radial neighbourhood; its reconstructed tail is nearly in the Galactic plane
controls: finite disc thickness and intrinsic ellipticity
dust path length and selection with inclination
spiral morphology, pitch angle and radial position
stellar population, age and carrier consistency
embedded Milky Way vantage versus external-galaxy viewing geometry
spiralInclinationSlicingTemplate.interpretation: a multi-galaxy inclination surface can scan a declared projection law, but cannot infer T1 until the mapping between the candidate axis and ordinary disc geometry is independently specified

corpusDerivedHypothesisTournament.angleStatus: numerical rehearsal: the ordinary tail-to-Galactic-normal angle is used as the hyperplane principal angle only in an explicitly declared normal-axis lift into four dimensions

relativeDegreesOfFreedomAudit.parameterization: n_G = cos(theta)*n_E + sin(theta)*u, with u a unit vector in E; E intersect G = E intersect u-perp
relativeDegreesOfFreedomAudit.normalAxisBranch: the measured 87.04-degree tail-to-disc-normal angle may be carried into theta only after declaring those ordinary vectors to be lifts of the two hyperplane normals
relativeDegreesOfFreedomAudit.result: theta fixes the compression strength but not which Milky-Way-frame direction is exceptional; physical landmarks prevent quotienting away the two-angle choice of u

uniqueDirectionScalarFrequencyProjection.result: for a carrier known to occupy the unique rotated direction, a near-quarter-turn cannot produce only a ppm-scale shift through the scalar kernel unless q is about 0.95 or an independent normalization cancels the order-one projection
uniqueDirectionScalarFrequencyProjection.scope: not a whole-object brightness law; two spatial directions are shared in the rank-two-plus-one frame model
uniqueDirectionScalarFrequencyProjection.status: unique-direction q=0 small-perturbation reading disfavoured; no carrier assignment is presently available

uniquePlaneTwoChannelRotation.model: two-component orthogonal rotation with conserved squared norm
uniquePlaneTwoChannelRotation.result: within the unique rotated two-plane a unitary channel rotation preserves norm but predicts an almost complete channel swap; the two common spatial directions are unchanged and total brightness alone cannot distinguish it
uniquePlaneTwoChannelRotation.status: open but unconfirmed; requires a phase-, polarization-, carrier- or gravity-sensitive second-channel reader
uniquePlaneTwoChannelRotation.typingBoundary: quarter-turn results on other corpus carriers do not establish this celestial transport law

rankTwoPlusOneSpatialFrameProjection.model: two three-dimensional subspaces of a four-dimensional ambient space with a guaranteed common two-plane
rankTwoPlusOneSpatialFrameProjection.covarianceIdentifiability: for every theta below 90 degrees and every observed positive-definite covariance, C_intrinsic = inverse(P)*C_observed*inverse(P)^T reproduces the observation; morphology alone cannot recover theta or u
rankTwoPlusOneSpatialFrameProjection.result: two directions transmit unchanged and one is compressed; the two-dimensional sky axis ratio cannot be compared directly with the three-dimensional condition number without the intrinsic covariance and viewing map
rankTwoPlusOneSpatialFrameProjection.status: non-identifying with present data; the earlier direct axis-ratio rejection is withdrawn

boundaryOrGradientMixing.evidence: retrospective held-out sharp-step, smooth-step, relaxation and localized-layer tournament
boundaryOrGradientMixing.result: all spatial forms improve on a constant offset but none is distinguishable from an ordinary linear tail term

corpusDerivedHypothesisTournament.verdict: present data neither confirm nor reject the rank-two-plus-one frame geometry; only a unique-direction scalar reading is constrained, and the exceptional singular direction has not been assigned to an observed carrier

authorityLimits: membership was preselected with convergent-point kinematics, so this is not independent discovery
a constant spectroscopic offset still does not identify configuration T1
no source-derived T1 law predicted the observed spatial slope before inspection
ordinary tail dynamics, binaries, atmosphere-dependent shifts and Gaia RV systematics are not yet removed

the completed linear-tail comparison is only a retrospective surrogate; the next gate requires the published N-body snapshot or equivalent frozen ordinary prediction, an independently derived theta(s) law if available, and untouched or independent spectroscopy

minimumSeparatingBundle: astrometric perspective or convergent-point radial velocity independent of spectral frequencies
spectroscopic systemic velocity with binary, atmospheric and instrument zero-point controls
preregistered multi-line or multi-carrier q law
jointly specified electromagnetic and gravitational kernels before mass comparison
controls: stellar gravitational redshift and convective line shifts
extinction, metallicity, rotation and stellar-model uncertainty

verdict.status: constant-angle single-channel hypothesis non-identifying; first cross-channel pass detects an unassigned spatial residual but does not identify T1
verdict.nextGate: replace inverse-parallax PCA with a full astrometric-covariance tail model, obtain frozen ordinary phase-space predictions, and test line-resolved or independent spectroscopy outside the present sample
